title: SRE observation logbook: QA playback and tail-signal notes
content:
Week window: 2029-11-13 -> 2029-11-19
Summary:
This entry is an "observation logbook" style weekly note: quick signal takeaways, an incident playback summary, SLO status snapshot, and the on-call handoff checklist we actually used. Tone is candid — contains hypotheses and open questions for follow-up.

Key incident (2029-11-16, 03:42 UTC): transient tail-latency spike affecting hosted-api text/generate route in eu-west1. Symptom chain: elevated 95/99th latency for >90s, automatic fallback to smaller model triggered, increased error-budget consumption for the day. Root-cause hypothesis: coordinated KV-cache churn during a longer-than-usual token-prefix pattern combined with a kernel selection edge-case on quantized model variant (v2-q4).
What we observed:
- Synthetic canary alarms fired at 03:41:22 UTC (p95 jump) and 03:41:35 UTC (p99).
- Autoscaler attempted to add nodes but some warm-up paths were blocked by a concurrency limiter; scale-up completed after ~70s.
- Fallback policy executed: routed a subset (~12%) of traffic to model-variant small-medium as designed.
- No data plane errors (5xx) persisted; most failures surfaced as timeouts at client gateways.

Detection and triage notes:
- Primary alert source: synthetic-run and latency-service trace aggregation.
- Quick triage: checked KV-cache eviction metrics, kernel error counters, and recent rollout tags. Found a flurry of cache_eviction events aligned with a burst of long-sequence requests from a single customer region.
- Cross-check with rollout metadata: a canary of v2-q4 was in a gradual ramp (10% region traffic) for eu-west1 at the time — suspect interplay.

Immediate mitigations executed:
- Throttled the customer-origin prefix to smooth incoming sequence-length distribution (rate-limit override).
- Rolled back the quantized variant to the previous stable build for eu-west1 (rollback completed by 04:05 UTC).
- Increased autoscaler aggressiveness for node warm-up in the eu-west1 pool for 10 minutes.

SLO snapshot (end of week):
- Text/generate availability (SLO target 99.95%): 99.88% for the week (error budget used: ~0.07%).
- Median latency target: met. P95/P99 drifted above target for 1.5 hours on incident window.
- Action: schedule a micro-postmortem and SLO alert tuning review to prevent noisy paging for short-lived regressions.

On-call handoff used (what worked / what didn't):
- What worked: fast detection from synthetic, runbook link in pager alert included the rollback command, shared dashboard provided immediate heatmap.
- What didn't: concurrency limiter and warm-up delays were not surfaced in runbook; escalation path to infra-kernel team took 23 minutes (too long).
- Handoff checklist appended to next-shift message: state, mitigations done, open hypotheses, required owners (infra-kernel, model-onboarding, customer-ops).

Action items and owners:
- SRE: produce 30-min micro-postmortem doc with timeline, log snippets, and hypothesis validation (owner: Evelyn Kim, due: 2029-11-23).
- Model infra: reproduce KV-cache churn scenario in staging and test kernel selection under quantized variant (owner: Ravi Menon, due: 2029-11-29).
- Console UX: add warm-up/warm-start signals to the autoscaler dashboard; add a circuit-breaker visible flag when fallback triggers (owner: María López, due: 2029-12-06).
- Customer success: follow up with impacted customer to coordinate prefix patterns and mitigation playbook (owner: Jonah Park, due: 2029-11-27).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Are there model-side cache-protection knobs we can flip to avoid mass-eviction during long-context bursts?
- Should fallback thresholds be dynamic by region to avoid excessive fallback during regional brief storms?
- Can the autoscaler advertise a predicted warm-up ETA in the dashboard to help triage?

Notes to next shift (short):
- Incident: eu-west1 latency spike -> rollback of v2-q4 completed; monitor p99 for 24h.
- Keep an eye on cache_eviction spikes correlated to long_token_count metric.
- If p99 crosses 2x baseline for >5min, escalate to infra-kernel immediately.

Appendix (useful artifacts):
- Quick links: JIRA SRE-2145 (investigation), Confluence ops-logbook-2029-11, GitHub infra PR #4521 (revert candidate), Slack thread #ops-bridge-thread-1209.
- Minimal timeline: 03:40: synth alarm -> 03:42: fallback -> 03:50: autoscale nodes in progress -> 04:05: rollback -> 04:12: p99 trending down.

Tone closure:
This entry is intentionally conversational; it's a set of observations to seed the postmortem and to make the next-hand-off faster. Please add comments inline or drop notes to #ops-bridge if you see anything missing or if you want to claim an action item.
